title: API Aggregation
description: Learn API aggregation patterns to combine data from multiple services into a single response.

data.text: API aggregation solves the problem of clients making multiple round-trips to fetch related data. Amazon and Netflix use aggregation extensively to reduce latency and simplify client code.

In a microservices system, a single page might require data from 5-10 services. If the client makes each call separately, latency adds up quickly. On a 3G network with 200ms round-trip time, 5 calls take 1 second just in network latency.

data.title: Aggregation Approaches
items: API Gateway aggregation: Gateway calls multiple services and combines responses
Backend for Frontend: Dedicated service aggregates for one client type
GraphQL: Client specifies exact data needs; server aggregates
Batch endpoints: Services expose batch endpoints for related resources

data.title: Aggregation Complexity
data.text: Aggregation adds complexity to the gateway or BFF. Avoid over-aggregating; keep the gateway lightweight and focused on cross-cutting concerns.

items.question: How is aggregation different from composition?
items.answer: They are similar. Aggregation usually implies combining data from multiple services. Composition is a broader term that can include calling services sequentially.

items.question: Should I aggregate in the gateway or in a BFF?
items.answer: Use the gateway for simple aggregation and cross-cutting concerns. Use a BFF for complex, client-specific aggregation.

items.question: What about GraphQL?
items.answer: GraphQL is excellent for aggregation because resolvers can fetch from multiple services. Many companies use GraphQL as their primary aggregation layer.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Aggregation reduces client round-trips and latency
Keep aggregation logic in BFFs for complex scenarios
GraphQL is a natural fit for aggregation
data.takeaway: Aggregate data at the edge to simplify clients and improve performance.
